Here’s a comprehensive overview of **Men’s Ski Cross at the 2018 Winter Olympics**, held in **PyeongChang, South Korea**, from **20–22 February 2018** at the **Bokwang Phoenix Park**:

---

### 🏅 **Event Overview**
- **Discipline**: Freestyle Skiing – Ski Cross  
- **Format**: Head-to-head, multi-rider (typically 4 per heat) elimination races down a technical, obstacle-filled course featuring jumps, banked turns, rollers, and narrow passages.  
- **Olympic Debut**: Ski cross debuted at the 2010 Vancouver Games; PyeongChang 2018 was its **third Olympic appearance**.  
- **Qualification**: Athletes raced in timed **qualifying runs**, with top 32 advancing to knockout rounds (1/8 finals). Qualifying times determined seeding for head-to-head bracket placement.

---

### 🥇 **Medalists**
| Medal | Athlete | Country | Time / Notes |
|-------|---------|---------|--------------|
| **🥇 Gold** | **Brady Leman** | Canada | Won final heat with aggressive, clean line and strong gate starts; first Canadian man to win Olympic ski cross gold. |
| **🥈 Silver** | **Marc Bischofberger** | Switzerland | Narrowly edged out in final; finished 0.13 seconds behind Leman. |
| **🥉 Bronze** | **Armin Niederer** | Switzerland | Overcame a crash in semifinals to win bronze medal race; Switzerland’s first-ever men’s ski cross Olympic medal (2 Swiss on podium). |

- **Notable Absence**: Defending Olympic champion **Jean-Frédéric Chapuis** (FRA), who won in Sochi 2014, crashed out in the 1/8 finals — a major upset.

---

### 📅 **Competition Schedule (PyeongChang Time, KST)**
- **20 Feb (Tue)**: Qualification (morning)  
- **21 Feb (Wed)**: 1/8 Finals, Quarterfinals, Semifinals  
- **22 Feb (Thu)**: Small Final (4th–6th place) and **Big Final (Medal Race)** at 20:30 KST  

*All races were held under clear, cold conditions — ideal for grip and visibility.*

---

### 🏔️ **Venue: Bokwang Phoenix Park**
- Purpose-built for PyeongChang; hosted all freestyle skiing and snowboard events.  
- Men’s ski cross course: ~1,050 m long, ~145 m vertical drop, ~12–15 sec average run time.  
- Featured 4–5 jumps, 6–8 banked turns, rollers, and narrow “choke points” demanding tactical positioning and drafting.

---

### 📊 **Key Stats & Highlights**
- **35 athletes** from **15 nations** competed.  
- **Canada** had its strongest-ever Olympic ski cross result — Leman’s gold plus teammate **Kevin Drury** finishing **4th** (0.03 seconds behind bronze).  
- **USA’s** top finisher was **Bryon Wilson**, who placed **13th** (eliminated in quarterfinals).  
- **France**, despite Chapuis’ early exit, still fielded a strong team: **Xavier Krief** (10th), **Thomas Klenke** (15th).  
- **Norway’s** **Kristoffersen brothers** — **Mikko** (6th) and **Sverre** (16th) — both advanced to semifinals; Mikko placed 6th overall.

---

### 🎯 **Notable Moments & Drama**
- **Leman’s Redemption Arc**: After finishing 4th in Sochi 2014 and missing the 2014–15 season due to injury, Leman returned stronger — winning the 2016–17 World Cup title and entering PyeongChang as favorite. His flawless final — holding the inside line through a critical banked turn — sealed his win.  
- **Swiss Sweep**: Armin Niederer’s bronze came after a dramatic semifinal crash — he recovered in time to win the small final, securing Switzerland’s first men’s ski cross podium.  
- **Controversy-Free Event**: Unlike previous Games, no major disqualifications or protests tainted the men’s event — all medal races were clean and decisive.  
- **Broadcast Innovation**: NBC and Eurosport used drone footage and real-time split timing, highlighting the sport’s intensity and technical nuance.

---

### 📈 **Historical Context & Legacy**
- This marked **Canada’s first men’s ski cross Olympic gold**, ending a 12-year drought in freestyle skiing golds (since Alex Bilodeau’s 2010 moguls win).  
- The 2018 result solidified **Brady Leman** as one of ski cross’s all-time greats — he retired from competition in 2022 after adding a second World Championship title (2019).  
- The race underscored the sport’s evolution: increased emphasis on technical consistency over pure speed, with drafting, gate starts, and cornering strategy as decisive factors.  
- Inspired growing participation in North America and Europe — especially in Switzerland, Canada, and France — leading to deeper talent pools for Beijing 2022 and beyond.

---

### 📚 Bonus: Fun Facts
- Leman wore **red-and-white ski boots** — a nod to the Canadian flag — and skied with a “B” logo on his helmet (for “Brady” and “Belief”).  
- The men’s and women’s ski cross finals were held on **consecutive nights**, providing a dramatic back-to-back showcase (Marielle Thompson won bronze for Canada in women’s event on 21 Feb).  
- PyeongChang was the **first Winter Olympics held in South Korea**, and ski cross was among the most-watched freestyle events — praised for its accessibility and excitement.

---

- Biographies of the medalists  
- Video highlights or official IOC links
